::: {.callout-tip title="How to render: the course default"}
1. Save the `.qmd` file you want to render, then open the **Command Palette** (**View → Command Palette**, or press **Ctrl+Shift+P** on Windows/Linux / **Cmd+Shift+P** on Mac) and run **Quarto: Render Document**. When a menu asks which format, choose **Render HTML** (or **Render PDF (Typst)** for a PDF). <!-- AI-EDIT(2026-06-22): REVIEW-row46 / D-003,GAP-R678-1 — added Command Palette keyboard shortcut (Ctrl+Shift+P / Cmd+Shift+P) so students can find it without hunting the menu -->
2. **Always-works fallback (terminal):** type the render command with the file's path as shown in the Explorer, for example:

   ```bash
   quarto render practice_report.qmd
   ```

   Always name the file — a bare `quarto render` rebuilds the *whole* project and takes much longer.
3. The **Preview** button at the top-right of the editor renders too, in the format the file asks for, without the menu.

**Where did the output go?** Watch the render log for the `Output created:` line — it names the exact file created. By default the file appears next to your `.qmd`; in projects that set an output directory (like this book's `docs/` folder), it appears there instead.

**To look at it,** click the file in the Explorer: an `.html` or `.pdf` opens in a tab inside VS Code. After you render again, close that tab and click the file again. To open it in your own browser instead (for example, slides to present full screen, or a page to print), right-click it and choose **Download**.
:::
